Care of the Normal Newborn

Care of the normal newborn — first minutes, examination, weight loss, immunisation schedule, feeding and hygiene.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe immediate care after birth
  • Perform a newborn examination
  • Explain the immunisation schedule
  • Give feeding and hygiene advice

In simple words

The newborn is in a period of rapid adjustment. Good care means airway, warmth, cord and eye care, safe feeding and early identification of problems.

Immediate care

  • Airway: clear the secretions, dry and stimulate
  • Warmth: skin-to-skin, keep the head covered, delay bath
  • Cord: sterile clamp and cut, keep clean and dry
  • Eyes: tetracycline ointment
  • Vitamin K 1 mg IM
  • APGAR scoring at 1 and 5 minutes
  • Identification band and weight
  • First feed within the first hour

Newborn examination

  • Weight — normal 2.5 to 3.5 kg; average loss of 5-10% in the first week, then regained
  • Head circumference — about 35 cm
  • Chest circumference — about 33 cm
  • Frontanelle — soft diamond-shaped; closes at 18 months
  • Temperature — 36.5 to 37.5 degrees C
  • Respirations — 30 to 60 per minute
  • Heart rate — 110 to 160 per minute
  • Skin — slightly blue hands and feet (acrocyanosis) common; jaundice at day 2 to 3 peaks by day 4; physiological jaundice disappears by day 7 to 10

Immunisation

Vaccine Schedule
BCG At birth or up to 1 year
Hepatitis B At birth, 6, 14 weeks
OPV and fIPV At birth, then 6, 10, 14 weeks
Pentavalent (DPT, Hib, Hep B) 6, 10, 14 weeks
Rotavirus 6, 10, 14 weeks
MR (measles-rubella) 9-12 months and 16-24 months

🔴 Keep the baby warm and feed on demand

The newborn loses heat quickly. Never give water, honey or sugar water. Feed the baby on demand; the baby should have at least 6 wet nappies a day.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. BCG, zero dose oral polio, hepatitis B and vitamin K at birth.
  2. Pentavalent is given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks.
  3. MR vaccine is given at 9-12 months and 16-24 months.
  4. Weight loss of 5-10% in the first week is normal.
  5. Exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months.
  6. Never give water or honey to a newborn.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Neonatal jaundice after day 1 needs phototherapy assessment.
  2. Overheating and undercooling both harm the baby.
  3. Place the baby on the back to sleep to prevent suffocation.
  4. The cord stump falls by 7-10 days.
  5. Wash your hands before every contact.

📌 Memory trick

BCG, OPV0 and Hep B at birth; Pentavalent at 6,10,14 weeks; MR at 9 months.

60-second revision

  • Immediate: airway, warmth, cord, eye drops, vitamin K, identify, APGAR.
  • Normal values: weight, heart rate, respiratory rate and temperature.
  • Immunisation: BCG, hepatitis B, OPV0, pentavalent, MR.
  • Feed on demand; no water; 6+ wet nappies per day.
  • Danger signs: poor feeding, fast breathing, cold or hot, jaundice day 1, convulsion.

Test yourself

Normal newborn weight is:

Answer: B. A normal newborn weighs about 2.5 to 3.5 kg.

The vaccine given at birth is:

Answer: B. BCG is given at birth (with hepatitis B and OPV zero).

Physiological jaundice appears at:

Answer: B. Physiological jaundice appears after 24 to 48 hours and settles by day 7 to 10; jaundice within 24 hours is pathological.

A newborn should have at least this many wet nappies a day:

Answer: C. Six or more wet nappies per day indicate adequate feeding.

To prevent sudden infant death, the baby should be placed:

Answer: B. Back sleeping is recommended for safe sleep.
